title: Python SDK: fan-in/fan-out typed stream iterator patterns for chat + event replays
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current Python SDK streaming primitives cover single-stream consume patterns but lack ergonomic building blocks for realistic application patterns: fan-in of multiple partial-event sources, fan-out to multiple sinks (e.g., UI, metrics, persistence), typed event unions and a simple replay/checkpoint API for resumability and tests. This makes consumer code verbose, error-prone, and inconsistent across teams.

Goal: Provide a concise, well-documented set of high-level primitives and compatibility helpers layered on existing low-level streaming APIs that let application engineers implement robust chat UIs, conversational persistence, and replayable test harnesses with minimal boilerplate.
proposal: Deliver a small API surface: (1) TypedEventIterator: an async iterator that yields typed event variants (TokenDelta, Meta, FinalCompletion, Error, Watermark). (2) FanInMerge: deterministic merge of multiple iterators with source tags and optional watermarking. (3) FanOutDemux: adapters to fan out events to multiple async sinks with backpressure hints. (4) CheckpointHandle: lightweight opaque token to persist and resume iterator state at message-level granularity. (5) Convenience builders: stream.to_ui(), stream.to_kv_cache(), stream.to_metrics() for common sinks. Provide examples and a test harness for deterministic replay from stored event logs.
implementation_notes:
Start by implementing a pure-Python reference for TypedEventIterator that wraps current stream event dicts and performs schema coercion. Add lightweight C-extension / Cython later only if hot path shows measurable cost. Use the runtime's existing streaming transport; avoid adding new wire protocols. Keep checkpoint token format stable: base64-encoded JSON with schema_version and last_event_id. Ensure tokens are forward-compatible by embedding schema_version. Add detailed unit tests using recorded SSE capture fixtures.

Telemetry: emit typed events for each consumer action (merge_started, merge_backpressure, checkpoint_saved, replay_started). Hook into SDK-level tracer and metrics.

Backward compatibility: provide adapter.from_raw_stream(stream) to keep existing user code working while enabling gradual migration.
